prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to give specific phone numbers and a short list of the best individual practices I should know where in Denver you want care (Denver is large) and whether you have a preferred insurance, budget, or timeline. Do you have a ZIP code or neighborhood, and will you use dental insurance or need financing?

While you decide, here are immediate, actionable recommendations so you can start calling right away, and what to ask each office and why.

Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): best for surgical aspects (implant placement, extractions, bone grafting, complex cases, IV sedation). Call an OMS if you anticipate bone grafts, sinus lifts, or IV sedation.
- Periodontists: specialists in gums and supporting structures; they frequently place implants and treat gum disease and bone loss.
- Prosthodontists or implant-restorative dentists: if you need complex restorative work (full-arch, esthetic anterior tooth replacement), a prosthodontist coordinates implant placement and the final crown/bridge.
- Large multidisciplinary implant centers or dental schools: good for complex cases, second opinions, teaching-faculty care (often lower cost at dental schools).

What to ask when you call (short checklist)
- Do you place dental implants? (If yes:) How many implant cases do you do per month?
- What is the clinician’s specialty and training (OMS, periodontist, prosthodontist)? Any fellowship or implant-specific training?
- Do you use CBCT 3D imaging onsite for planning?
- Which implant brands do you use and why? (High-quality systems include Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer/BioHorizons — you don’t need all details, but reputable clinicians use established systems.)
- Do you do the surgery and restoration in-house or refer the crown to another dentist?
- What sedation options do you offer (local, oral, IV)?
- Typical timeline and steps (consult, imaging, surgery, healing time, restoration)
- Rough cost range for a single implant including crown, and financing options
- Any warranties or guarantees on implants/ restorations
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references or online reviews?

How to narrow choices quickly
- Prioritize board-certified oral surgeons or board-certified periodontists for surgical complexity.
- Prefer practices that use CBCT for planning and have in-house restorations or good coordination with your restorative dentist.
- Read recent patient reviews for implant-specific feedback, not just general dentistry reviews.
- Ask your general dentist for referrals — they commonly refer to local specialists they trust and can coordinate the crown.

If you want, I can:
- Find 4–6 specific clinics close to your ZIP code (with phone numbers, short notes on each) and rank them by specialty, patient reviews, and whether they accept your insurance.
- Or produce a script with exact wording to use on the phone.

Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you have dental insurance (and which plan) and I’ll pull a targeted list of practices in Denver to call.
